quaesitor/measurements.html.one_line: The most substantive Quaesitor text, with real tables and a clean before-and-after documentation comparison with exact tests, but written as a first-person pitch with several numbers in the prose that contradict its own tables or the run data, a mislabelled model column, no limits section and private data.

dimensions.question: Implicit: how two assistants split non-correct answers between declining and silent errors. Not placed against any external literature ('Every text-to-SQL benchmark reports accuracy' with no citation).
dimensions.design: Planted traps, verified hand-written queries, 15 languages x 3 repeats, rule-based classification; one verdict per question-language cell. The aggregation of three repeats into one cell verdict is not described. Model identities appear only as aliases opus/sonnet; sampling temperature and seed not recorded (per silent-detector).
dimensions.evidence: Table 1 (retail, subscriptions) matches the comparison tables except sonnet/subscriptions, which recomputes to 126/38/85/3 from the files now in the repository (Czech run has 1 repeat) against the published 135/41/91/3. Table 2's 'A / B' header is wrong: every row is sonnet/opus while table 1 defines A = opus. Prose: 'both models were silently wrong four times in five' on taxi is false (sonnet 80 %, opus 70 %); 'declined 59 times on my retail pack' contradicts table 1 (55); 'declined zero times here' contradicts the taxi comparison tables (opus 8 of 80). Facts card '55 vs 1, same questions, same correct count' is false (40 vs 28 correct). Documentation result: exact McNemar p = 1.00 and sign test p = 0.0023 on 22 questions are reported properly; 'replicated three times' counts the headline run as a replication.
dimensions.data_code: quaesitor repository private; original pages carry SHA-256 run fingerprints but no reader can rebuild any number. detector.json is public and carries the total answer count.
dimensions.limits: One limits paragraph for the documentation run only; nothing on planted vs production data, tiny n outside retail (10-80 cells per model), no intervals, unrecorded temperature, private data.
dimensions.references: Seven references, six of them the author's own original pages; r7 never cited in the body; no access dates; no external literature on text-to-SQL evaluation or abstention.
dimensions.form: Kicker without kind; slogan h1 and multi-sentence deck; slogan headings ('The query ran. The answer was zero. Nobody had any customers that month.', 'Two models, one score, two personalities'); no short version, metadata block or change log.

quaesitor/taxonomy.html.one_line: A useful catalogue that isolates each fault and reports the median error it produced, but its access section presents twelve designed scenarios as twelve observed leaks, which the one recorded run contradicts, and it closes on slogans.

dimensions.question: Stated in the deck as an anecdote ('Everyone in data has an anecdote') rather than as a question against prior work.
dimensions.design: Sound isolation: verified and naive queries differ only at the trap. Medians pooled across models, languages and packs without saying so.
dimensions.evidence: Catalogue table as published (medians over 6-44 runs). Facts card 'median divergence ≈ 10 %, nearly half below that' is a tautology: half of all values are below a median by definition. Access section: 'in all twelve the answer arrived with rows the asker was not entitled to' is contradicted by method/outputs/access_sonnet.md (20 August 2026, sonnet, one attempt each): 9 passed, 1 leak (A11), 1 flagged for review (A03: 1 985 vs 1 909), 1 unmeasured (A04). 'This is the most common bypass in practice' (A02) is unsupported.

quaesitor/why.html.one_line: An argument essay titled with its own untested thesis ('Trust grows faster than accuracy'), promotional in tone, with a claim that the harness is open when the repository is private and several misreadings of the external sources it leans on.

dimensions.question: The thesis (checking falls as accuracy rises) is asserted in the title, deck and body; no Quaesitor run measures user checking behaviour, so it is untested.
dimensions.design: The five-step verification method is described clearly and is the strongest part.
dimensions.evidence: External claims checked 29 September 2026: BEAVER 10.8 % / 30.1 % / 9 128 correct, but 'scores in the eighties on public benchmarks' is not in the source and the 10.8 % is for an agentic framework using GPT-5.2; Chen et al. report the semantic agent had 65.7 % higher precision, not that the broader agent was '65.7 % less precise'; Zhu et al.'s ~69K instances are per backbone; Cube figures correct (50.5→67.7, 46.5→68.7, 45.5→68.7) with CIs the page omits; Omni's 4 602 / 81.2 % is a secondary report; Ghosh 271 049 / 154 050 correct; Bajaj 53 % correct; Julka 59 %/42 % correct; quaesitor-zero is v0.1.5 on PyPI, not v0.1.4. CACM blog and Ar-Spider DOI refuse automated access and were not re-read. Own claim 'The harness that produced them, open' is false: the repository is private (r17 itself says private). The 95 attempts returning 684 recomputes: on the cohort question (retail Q10, verified 621) the standard sonnet and opus runs (retail in 15 languages plus benchmark_v0 Czech) returned 684 in 95 answers; the two confidence-prompt runs (agent_opus-conf_cs, agent_sonnet-conf_cs, 24 August) add 6 more, which is the raw count of 101 (checked 29 September 2026).
dimensions.limits: None; the essay claims 'none of this was my claim to make' while resting the headline on its own untested argument.
dimensions.references: 18 entries, no access dates, 'ibid.' entry, BEAVER dated 2026 though first posted 2024.
dimensions.form: No kind in kicker; five-sentence deck; bold lead-ins in running text; slogans and closing morals throughout; 'It is the one I am proudest of'; the Roman-magistrate paragraph is brand copy.
